Press review: US threatens Iran with sanctions as Trump steps up trade war with Canada
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
10:00:01 UTC
19:00:01 KST

MOSCOW, August 24. /TASS/. The US vows to unleash "unprecedented" economic pressure on Iran; Ukrainians have "opened Pandora’s box" by striking Russian civilian infrastructure; and the US and Canada engage in a trade war. These stories topped Monday’s newspaper headlines across Russia.
Izvestia: US threatens Iran with new sanctions
The US is preparing new sanctions against Iran, the details of which the Treasury will unveil on August 24. Meanwhile, Trump's announcement of "unprecedented" economic pressure does not exclude new military scenarios. Talks between Washington and Tehran remain at an impasse as the 60-day memorandum expired on August 17 and the two sides have yet to reach a final accord.
Moscow has traditionally advocated for the parties to resume dialogue. Moreover, it is ready to participate in mediation efforts if requested to do so, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Alimov told Izvestia. "If requested, Russia is ready to support mediation efforts to end the aggression against Iran and maintain stability in the Middle East. This includes the updated security concept for the Persian Gulf that we are promoting," the senior diplomat noted.
Moscow’s proposals on security in the Persian Gulf remain pertinent, Middle East expert Grigory Lukyanov recalled. They are based on the participation of all regional countries and the principle of indivisible security. However, the main problem is the absence of trust between the parties. Moreover, under Trump, the US is unwilling to recognize other states as legitimate mediators or guarantors of agreements.
Nevertheless, mediation by third countries remains in demand. Middle Eastern countries, as well as European and Asian energy importers, are particularly interested in stabilizing the situation as soon as possible. However, their ability to influence the US position is limited. According to Lukyanov, progress can only be achieved through confidential negotiations and by seeking compromises on specific issues.
However, the US and Iran have not abandoned negotiations, Lukyanov emphasized. However, both sides are confident in their strong positions and are unwilling to make concessions. At the same time, the protracted conflict creates problems for both Washington and Tehran. Iran needs external financial resources, while the US is facing the consequences of rising energy prices and problems with transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
Izvestia: What to expect after Putin’s harsh statements on Ukraine
Moscow will no longer give in to the West’s empty promises: peace talks remain a separate track from the Russian army’s military operations. Vladimir Putin has clearly set out the conditions for discussing an end to the conflict. By striking civilian infrastructure, the Ukrainians have, as the Russian leader noted, "opened Pandora’s box" - and the response will be "severe." At the same time, Kiev’s peace "proposals" merely mimic peacemaking approaches, experts said.
"All of Kiev’s actions are aimed not at peace talks, but rather at escalating the conflict. That much is clear," former Ukrainian Prime Minister Nikolay Azarov told Izvestia. According to Ukrainian lawmaker Spiridon Kilinkarov, Kiev has been trying to escalate tensions since spring. Ukraine continues to cling to a single scenario: freezing the fighting and rearming. Moscow, however, does not accept this option. Kilinkarov emphasized that substantive negotiations are unlikely to begin before mid-September unless Ukraine puts forward new proposals. He noted that a peaceful settlement by the end of the year is unlikely.
"There have been no diplomatic proposals from Kiev on a mutual cessation of attacks. Moscow is being asked only to unilaterally stop its strikes," Bogdan Bezpalko, a member of the Russian Presidential Council for Interethnic Relations, noted. According to the expert, Zelensky needs the escalation for domestic political stability. Therefore, there are no signs of progress toward resolving the conflict in the Kiev regime's actions.
The upcoming European elections are also hindering the negotiations. According to another Ukrainian lawmaker Vladimir Oleynik, Europe is far from monolithic in its backing of Kiev: Slovakia and Hungary do not directly support the conflict, while in Germany and France, the current governments are afraid to admit it is a losing battle, otherwise they would have to explain to voters where their taxes have gone. Therefore, in his opinion, European governments will "drag their feet until the very last moment," but as new election cycles approach, their support for Kiev will become increasingly unstable.
Vedomosti: Reasons behind Donald Trump’s new trade war with Canada
After failing to reach a trade deal with Ottawa, President Donald Trump imposed 50% tariffs on some of Canada’s exports to the US. These measures had been announced in late July but were delayed until August 19 in an attempt to resolve the issues through diplomacy. Ultimately, however, the negotiations failed. Canada is preparing retaliatory measures that will take effect on September 8.
The US tariffs will apply to Canadian alcohol, dairy products, various types of paper, hockey equipment, cement, honey, seaweed, seeds, and automobiles. According to the Office of the US Trade Representative, the new tariffs will affect Canadian goods totaling $20 billion by the end of July, nearly 5% of Canada’s total exports to the US. Meanwhile, according to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, US tariffs will affect goods totaling $28 billion.
Despite their limited scope, the tariffs will affect both American consumers and Canadian exporters, Vladimir Pavlov, a senior research fellow at the MGIMO Institute of International Studies, told Vedomosti. The expert emphasized, however, that Canada has plans in place to shift its exports toward Asia and Europe. "The main problem here is simply that it will take time to implement these plans," Pavlov said. He also noted that the Trump administration should expect lawsuits and protests.
For Trump, the political logic behind continuing the trade war with Canada lies in maintaining his position at a time when the Canadian economy is not only withstanding the test of endurance under tariff pressure, but is also effectively retaliating, thereby harming the US economy, Pavel Koshkin, a senior researcher at the US and Canadian Studies Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences, said. "For the US president, backing down would mean admitting he was wrong and appearing weak, which he cannot afford amid the congressional election race and fluctuations in his approval ratings," the expert pointed out. According to Koshkin, tariffs are a tool that Trump has no intention of abandoning, as he considers them his primary means of exerting pressure across nearly all areas of foreign policy.
Rossiyskaya Gazeta: How Russia can restructure its oil exports in light of risks in Black Sea
Russian oil exports from the port of Novorossiysk on the Black Sea fell by half in the first half of August, from the usual 0.8-1 million barrels per day to 0.4 million barrels. The reason for this decline is the heightened risk to shipping due to drone attacks on tankers and port infrastructure, traders noted.
The situation around Russian oil exports via the Black Sea is not a localized disruption but rather systemic pressure on one of the key supply channels, NEFT Research External Communications Director Dmitry Prokofiyev told Rossiyskaya Gazeta. Novorossiysk, through which Russian Urals and Siberian Light crude, as well as Kazakhstan’s KEBCO, pass, has found itself at the epicenter of a logistical crisis. The expert emphasized that not a single shipment of crude was loaded at the port during the third week of August.
The port in Novorossiysk was adapted for loading oil onto tankers in the 1960s. At one time, most of the Soviet Union’s oil exports passed through it. However, in the 21st century, Russian shipments have largely moved to the Baltic Sea (the ports of Primorsk and Ust-Luga). Initially, European countries were the main buyers of Russian oil and petroleum products. However, after the EU embargo on Russian oil imports in 2022, the situation changed. Russia began shipping oil to Asia, yet the distribution of shipment volumes across export ports stayed unchanged. Loading volumes at the Baltic ports remained high.
That is precisely why it is impossible to redirect all Black Sea oil exports to the Baltic route. Terminal capacity is limited, Maxim Malkov, a Kept partner and head of the firm’s oil and gas practice, emphasized. However, the expert noted that there is significant flexibility between these routes. According to Prokofiyev, about 100,000 barrels per day can be rerouted, and this is already taking place.
The expert also emphasized that the paradox is that shipments from Novorossiysk to China and India have now become more expensive than those from the Baltic, despite the drop in volumes. In mid-August, transporting oil from the Baltic to northern China cost $17.6 per barrel, while shipping from Novorossiysk cost $24.7. This premium is for security, not distance. Shipping costs to western India from Novorossiysk increased by 43.5%, and to northern China by 22.7%. The reason is higher insurance and operational risks. If these risks disappear, shipments from Novorossiysk will be significantly cheaper than those from the Baltic.
Rossiyskaya Gazeta: Reasons behind central banks actively increasing their gold reserves, and how Russia responds to this trend
Central bank demand for gold in the second quarter of 2026 increased by 62% compared to the same period last year. According to experts, interest in gold bars among regulators and investors is growing while demand for jewelry is falling.
"There are several reasons for the growth in central banks’ demand for gold. The first is ongoing geopolitical tensions. The second is risks associated with the US dollar and the US economy. The third is reserve diversification, which involves reducing the share of fiat currencies and other types of assets in favor of the traditional 'safe haven,' including physical gold bars," cryptocurrency, compliance and sanctions risks expert Viktor Pershikov told Rossiyskaya Gazeta.
Professor Konstantin Pozdnyakov, an advisor to the Russian State Social University rector, also linked regulators’ growing interest in gold to the geopolitical situation. According to him, the freezing of certain countries’ reserves has made it clear to many central banks that the dollar and the euro are not completely reliable assets, despite their convenience. "Gold, on the other hand, cannot be frozen by sanctions, and that is precisely why demand for it is rising along with the level of global turmoil," the expert added.
Meanwhile, the high price of gold is weighing on the jewelry market. Demand for jewelry has fallen to 278 tons, the lowest level since the pandemic began. Manufacturers must account for the rising cost of the metal but cannot raise prices too much without losing customers, Pozdnyakov pointed out.
According to Pershikov, the Russian market is seeing two trends simultaneously in this situation. On the one hand, private investors continue to show growing interest in gold. In the second quarter, demand for gold bars and investment coins rose by 10% year-over-year. On the other hand, during the same period, the Bank of Russia reduced its gold reserves by approximately 22 tons, making it the largest seller of gold among central banks worldwide. "I wouldn’t interpret this as a decline in confidence in gold, since in Russia’s case, the sales are largely related to reserve rebalancing, liquidity, and budgetary operations," the expert stressed.
TASS is not responsible for the material quoted in these press reviews

Why Choose a Multiuse Air Purifier?
Small-apartment dwellers need a multipurpose air purifier for a practical reason: space. These compact appliances handle two or more tasks to maximize efficiency, while possibly saving you money too. They also reduce cords, the need for outlets, and storage space when the machine is not in use during off-seasons. Or maybe you're more aesthetically driven and want something that looks cool in the space rather than a clunky, large air purifier.
How I Tested
I tested each model for nearly a month, moving it around my house to test in different locations: when cooking on my unventilated gas stove, under my living room window that draws in a lot of building and exhaust fumes, and outside my cat's litter box. I measured whether and when the air purifier auto-engages, and how long it takes to return to clean air quality. I also used an air quality monitor to check for pollutants and the purifiers' efficacy, and a decibel monitor app on my phone to measure noise level when the appliance is on high. I also tested each setting, paying special attention to the multipurpose features and whether they were actually useful or just gimmicky. When another tester reviews a machine, they use the same metrics.
What I Look For in a Dual-Purpose Air Purifier
One of the main things I considered when testing was whether the extra features were actually useful. Each recommendation on the list has been deemed successful in both air purification and its other marketed “dual-purpose” function. I also considered size and purification ability—that's why the fun terrarium isn't a top pick; while it's super cute, it's not as effective as an air purifier.

California to seek TV channel sales from Paramount: Report
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
09:58:11 UTC
18:58:11 KST

Berk Kutay Gokmen
24 August 2026•Update: 24 August 2026
California Attorney General Rob Bonta is expected to ask Paramount to divest some TV channels and keep its movie studio separate from Warner Bros. as conditions for approving the $81 billion merger, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal on Sunday.
Bonta and Paramount CEO David Ellison are scheduled to meet Monday to discuss potential settlements to an antitrust lawsuit filed last month by California and 11 other states seeking to block the merger.
Lawyers for both sides met Friday to prepare for the talks, including discussions about Paramount’s cable and film businesses, according to the report.
The states argue the deal would create excessive concentration in theatrical movies and cable television, while also raising concerns about film and television production and employment.
Pressure is growing for the sides to reach an agreement. California Gov. Gavin Newsom and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass have recently urged them to find common ground.
Paramount faces significant financial pressure to close the transaction. Warner’s agreement includes a “ticking fee” requiring payments of about $650 million per quarter to Warner shareholders beginning Oct. 1. If the trial proceeds as planned, Paramount could owe more than $1 billion.
Paramount has also indicated it could leave California if no agreement is reached before the fee begins, with Tennessee reportedly its preferred alternative.
 
Bonta has insisted on structural remedies, while Paramount has committed to 30 theatrical releases annually but has resisted selling assets or accepting management restrictions that could reduce merger-related savings.

On 24 August, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy conferred the honorary distinction "Gratitude of the Ukrainian People" upon the people of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
Source: a presidential decree published on Ukraine's Independence Day, as reported by European Pravda
Details: According to the decree, the distinction was conferred for the solidarity and support shown to the Ukrainian people in their resistance to the armed aggression of the Russian Federation, the fight to preserve the nation, and the defence of Ukraine's statehood and shared civilisational values – humanity, freedom and peace.
The Gratitude of the Ukrainian People is a new distinction: Zelenskyy signed the decree establishing it on 20 August.
The decree states that the distinction is intended to express the respect and gratitude of the people of Ukraine to the people of a foreign state for solidarity and support of Ukraine in its resistance to Russian aggression and defence of statehood and shared civilisational values.
This includes support through the provision of military, humanitarian and financial aid and political support, as well as refuge for citizens of Ukraine.
The people of Britain have thus become the first to receive Ukraine's new honorary distinction since its establishment.

Russia's Chief of the General Staff Gerasimov served with notice of suspicion over Russian strike on Kyiv that killed 20 people
Kyiv • UNN
The Prosecutor General's Office notified Valery Gerasimov of the suspicion over the attack on Kyiv on July 2, 2026. Twenty civilians were killed and 32 were injured.
The Chief of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces, Valery Gerasimov, has been notified of suspicion over Russia’s strike on Kyiv on July 2, in which 20 people were killed. This is reported by the press service of the Prosecutor General’s Office, UNN reports.
Details
According to the Prosecutor General’s Office, on July 2, 2026, the Russian Armed Forces launched a massive combined attack on Kyiv and the Kyiv region using cruise and ballistic missiles and attack drones. As a result of the attack, 20 civilians were killed and another 32 were injured. Residential buildings, medical facilities, and civilian infrastructure were damaged and destroyed.
It was established that the strike on Kyiv was carried out pursuant to directives issued by the Chief of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces—the First Deputy Minister of Defense of the Russian Federation, who has simultaneously held the position of commander of the Joint Group of Forces of the Russian Armed Forces since January 11, 2023, the Prosecutor General’s Office noted.
"Since the beginning of the full-scale invasion, the general, acting in collusion with Russia’s highest political and military leadership, has issued operational directives and combat orders through subordinate military command bodies concerning systematic massive strikes on populated areas and civilian facilities throughout Ukraine," the Prosecutor General’s Office stated.
The Prosecutor General’s Office emphasized that the purpose of such attacks is to intimidate the civilian population, destroy critical infrastructure, and create humanitarian instability in order to exert pressure on Ukraine’s military and political leadership.
Based on the evidence collected, the general was notified of suspicion of violating the laws and customs of war, resulting in the deaths of people (Article 438 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine). In 2024, the International Criminal Court also issued a warrant for his arrest in connection with systematic strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure facilities
Background
Law enforcement officers launched an investigation into Russia’s missile-and-drone attack on Kyiv on July 2. According to the investigation, direct responsibility for organizing the attack lies with the Chief of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces and First Deputy Minister of Defense of the Russian Federation, Valery Gerasimov.

Ajit Doval in Beijing: India-China border talks set for August 25; what's on agenda?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
09:54:00 UTC
18:54:00 KST

NSA Ajit Doval arrives in Beijing for India-China border talks. Representative image: ANI
NEW DELHI: India's national security adviser Ajit Doval arrived in Beijing on Monday for a two-day visit. He is set to hold the 25th round of Special Representatives' Talks on the India-China boundary question with Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi on Tuesday. The visit comes as New Delhi and Beijing seek to build on recent signs of a thaw in ties.The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said Doval arrived in Beijing "at the invitation of Wang Yi".The talks come amid efforts by the two sides to gradually normalise relations following years of tensions along their disputed Himalayan border.
"The NSA will also call on China's vice president Han Zheng during his visit," the MEA said.
Boundary question and border stability on the agenda
The central focus of the talks will be the unresolved India-China boundary issues, with both sides expected to discuss the management of differences and the preservation of peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control.Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said the two sides would continue discussions in accordance with agreements reached by their leaders.India and China share a roughly 3,500-kilometre disputed border.
Relations came under severe strain after the deadly military clash in eastern Ladakh in 2020, following which the two sides held repeated military and diplomatic talks to address the situation.The latest Special Representatives’ meeting comes against the backdrop of a broader effort to stabilise the relationship.
Recent thaw in ties
Doval's Beijing visit follows his meeting with Wang in New Delhi in June on the sidelines of the BRICS National Security Advisers' meeting.The MEA described those discussions as part of the process of rebuilding bilateral ties.According to MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, the two sides "reviewed recent developments in bilateral relations and noted progress towards gradual normalisation".Jaiswal said Doval had stressed the importance of maintaining a stable relationship."NSA underlined that stable, predictable and constructive bilateral relations contribute to building trust and better understanding between the two sides," he said, adding: "The discussions were constructive and forward-looking."The latest visit also comes after subsequent meetings between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese president Xi Jinping on the sidelines of major international summits.At the SCO Summit in Tianjin last year, PM Modi and Xi welcomed what the two sides described as positive momentum and steady progress in bilateral relations following their previous meeting in Kazan in October 2024.
The two leaders had also reaffirmed that India and China were development partners rather than rivals, and that differences between them should not be allowed to become disputes."A stable relationship and cooperation between India and China and their 2.8 billion peoples on the basis of mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity are necessary for the growth and development of the two countries, as well as for a multipolar world and a multi-polar Asia befitting the trends of the 21st century," the MEA had said in a statement after the leaders' meeting.The Special Representatives’ mechanism has been one of the key diplomatic channels for addressing the boundary dispute between India and China. The 25th round comes at a time when both governments are seeking to consolidate the recent improvement in relations without setting aside their differences over the border.
For New Delhi, maintaining a stable and predictable relationship with Beijing is also significant as India prepares for the BRICS summit next month, where it hopes Xi will attend.

Another night of strikes on Ozon: Ukraine hit three logistics hubs overnight
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
12:53:32 EEST
18:53:32 KST

Another night of strikes on Ozon: Ukraine hit three logistics hubs overnight
Kyiv • UNN
On the night of August 24, three major Ozon logistics centers in Adygea, Stavropol Krai, and Dagestan came under attack. A series of attacks on the infrastructure of the Russian marketplace has continued for the third consecutive day.
During the night of August 24, Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck three major Ozon logistics hubs at once: in Enem, Nevinnomyssk, and Tyube. Fire Point co-owner and chief designer Denys Shtilerman confirmed the use of the company’s weapons. This is already the third consecutive day of strikes on the infrastructure of the Russian marketplace, UNN reports.
In Enem, Adygea, a logistics center covering approximately 91,200 square meters was attacked. The facility handles the reception, sorting, storage, and further distribution of goods in the south of the Russian Federation.
In Nevinnomyssk, Stavropol Krai, a hub covering approximately 93,500 square meters was struck. It is used for storing, sorting, assembling, and shipping Ozon orders.
The largest of the three facilities is located in Tyube, Dagestan. The total area of the logistics complex is approximately 130,000 square meters. It is one of Ozon’s key hubs in the North Caucasus, developed, among other things, in connection with the international North–South Transport Corridor.
Thus, more than 314,000 square meters of the Russian marketplace’s logistics facilities came under attack in a single night.
The nighttime attack on August 24 is a continuation of a series of strikes on Ozon’s logistics infrastructure, which has already lasted for three consecutive days. On the morning of August 23, an FP-1 attack drone manufactured by Fire Point struck an Ozon logistics complex in Orenburg.
A day earlier, on August 22, FP-1 drones struck the company’s logistics hub in Chapayevsk, Samara Oblast. It was one of Ozon’s largest centers in the Volga region: after all phases were launched, its area was expected to be approximately 135,000 square meters, its capacity more than 40 million goods, and its throughput over 215,000 orders per day.
Thus, while one large Ozon facility was hit on August 22 and 23, the attack on the night of August 24 already targeted three logistics hubs at once in different regions of Russia.
After Wildberries, it was Ozon’s turn
The Ministry of Defense of Ukraine explained the logic behind the strikes on Russia’s logistics infrastructure. The ministry stressed that such hubs are used, among other things, to store dual-use goods, and that their systematic destruction complicates Russian logistics and creates additional pressure on the economy of the Russian Federation.
Before this, Ukraine had struck more than 15 of Wildberries’ largest logistics hubs. For Russia, each such strike means not only the loss or suspension of warehouse space. Russian companies have to restructure routes, redistribute cargo among other centers, and spend additional resources protecting rear logistics—the very logistics that, until recently, Russia considered beyond the reach of Ukrainian weapons.

DAMASCUS, Syria (AP) — A former Islamic religious leader was sentenced to life in prison on Monday in the latest Syrian court trial of officials affiliated with the rule of ex-President Bashar Assad.
Former grand mufti Ahmad Badreddine Hassoun, an Assad loyalist who was vocally in support of the government’s policies, was convicted of inciting violence and justifying murder. He held the position of mufti from 2005 to 2021, when the position was abolished.
Judge Fakhreddine al-Aryan, head of the Fourth Criminal Court in Damascus, said the official religious establishment under Assad’s rule had “justified the use of barrel bombs that targeted civilian areas and caused widespread destruction, which constitutes a violation of the rules of international humanitarian law.”
Several other senior Assad-era officials -- including Assad himself and his brother, Maher -- have been sentenced to death in recent weeks, many of them in absentia. Hassoun was in custody and present in the court.
Some human rights groups have expressed concerns that the trials are being rushed and are potentially unfair, but the sentences have been welcomed by many Syrians who had previously expressed frustration that the new government was not moving with enough speed or strength against Assad-era figures.
Mass anti-government protests erupted in Syria in 2011 and were met by a brutal government crackdown, spiraling into a nearly 14-year civil war that left about half a million people dead and displaced more than half of Syria’s prewar population of 23 million.

Ozon Logistics Complex Hit for Second Time in a Row in Ukrainian Drone Attack on Orenburg
Unknown

- Category

Ozon Logistics Complex Hit for Second Time in a Row in Ukrainian Drone Attack on Orenburg
Overnight August 23, Ukrainian drones attacked the Russian city of Orenburg, with debris from intercepted UAVs falling on an Ozon logistics complex and causing a fire, according to local authorities and independent Russian Telegram channel ASTRA.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Orenburg Mayor Albert Yumadilov said several drones had been intercepted over the Orenburzhye special economic zone, which hosts a number of industrial facilities. No casualties were reported.
“Several UAVs were shot down over the special economic zone, where our industrial enterprises are located. Fortunately, no one was injured. Debris fell on the territory of the Ozon logistics complex, causing a fire that was quickly extinguished by Emergency Situations Ministry personnel,” Yumadilov said.
ASTRA reported that its OSINT analyst examined eyewitness footage from the area and identified a fire engine traveling toward the Ozon warehouse within the Orenburzhye special economic zone.
According to the Telegram channel, Ozon opened the first phase of the logistics complex in August 2024, with an initial floor area of approximately 40,000 square meters. A second phase was scheduled to open in spring 2025, potentially doubling the facility’s size.
“The logistics complex was expected to accommodate more than 31 million goods and process up to 915,000 orders per day,” ASTRA reported.
Ozon is among Russia’s largest e-commerce platforms, offering a broad range of products, from consumer goods and electronics to industrial equipment, through a marketplace model comparable to Amazon.
The platform also lists items that can have dual-use or military applications, such as drones and related components, communications systems, thermal-imaging equipment, and tactical gear. Some of these products have reportedly been procured for Russian forces fighting against Ukraine.
Investment in the facility exceeded 4 billion rubles (around $48 million), with plans to create more than 1,000 jobs, according to the outlet.
Following the drone attack, Ozon said more than 300 employees had been evacuated from the logistics center. The company temporarily suspended deliveries to the warehouse, while goods stored at the facility were removed from listings on its marketplace.
Ukrainian Defense Forces struck an Ozon logistics complex for the first time and also targeted the Novokuybyshevsk Oil Refinery in Russia’s Samara region, causing major fires at both sites, Ukrainian defense technology company Fire Point confirmed on August 22.
The incident comes a day after Ukrainian Defense Forces struck another Ozon logistics complex for the first time, alongside the Novokuybyshevsk Oil Refinery in Russia’s Samara region. Both facilities were hit by Ukrainian drones, triggering major fires.

The Commission said the latest approval was in addition to 16 billion euros (18.67 billion dollars) in previously approved procurement plans, of which 8.35 billion euros (9.75 billion dollars) has been disbursed.

BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- China's National Meteorological Center (NMC) on Monday issued blue alerts for typhoons and severe convective weather and a yellow alert for rainstorms, with multiple typhoons forecast to bring heavy rainfall and strong winds to parts of the country.
The China Meteorological Administration also raised its emergency response for major meteorological disasters from Level IV to Level III around Monday noon.

It is expected to track eastward from Monday night and then travel northward at a speed of 5 to 10 kilometers per hour, gradually approaching the coastal areas from Guangxi to the western Leizhou Peninsula in Guangdong Province, according to the NMC.
China's National Development and Reform Commission has allocated 50 million yuan (about 7.37 million U.S. dollars) in the central budget to support emergency recovery in Guangxi, where Typhoon Narra has already brought severe rainfall and floods.
The fund will focus on restoring damaged roads, water infrastructure, schools and hospitals to help resume normal production and daily life as soon as possible, according to the commission.
Typhoon Gaenari, the 20th typhoon of the year, made landfall along the coast of Quanzhou in east China's Fujian Province at around 12:30 p.m. on Monday, the local meteorological observatory said.
Meanwhile, the NMC said Typhoon Saudel, this year's 18th typhoon, is expected to enter the East China Sea on Wednesday and gradually approach the coastal areas of east China.
The NMC has advised local governments to take precautionary measures.
China has a four-tier color-coded weather warning system, with red representing the most severe, followed by orange, yellow and blue. ■

Swiss logistics billionaire Klaus-Michael Kühne has died

Swiss logistics billionaire Klaus-Michael Kühne has died
Swiss logistics billionaire Klaus-Michael Kühne died in the early hours of Monday morning at the age of 89. The company he helped to build into a global logistics heavyweight, Kühne+Nagel, announced the news.
Kühne was a member of the board of directors and the majority shareholder of the group. His holding company also holds shares in, amongst others, Lufthansa, the shipping company Hapag-Lloyd, the chemical logistics firm Brenntag, the rail and bus operator Flix, and the Hamburg football club HSV.
“With the death of Klaus-Michael, we have lost a visionary, a great entrepreneur and a remarkable individual,” said Jörg Wolle, Kühne+Nagel chair.
+ How Switzerland attracts the super rich
Kühne was a logistics expert through and through. Following a commercial apprenticeship, he joined the family business Kühne+Nagel in 1958 at the age of 21. In 1966 he became managing director and retained operational responsibility for decades. Later, he served as chair of the board of directors and, most recently, as a non-executive director.
Fortune heading to foundation
Over the course of all those years, what had been a Germany-focused freight forwarder evolved into a global logistics group. “My ambition was to create a global organisation. That took decades,” he once said in an interview.
Kühne was born in Hamburg in 1937 and emigrated to Switzerland with his father in the late 1960s. He ran his business empire from Schindellegi, Schwyz, in central Switzerland¨.
According to Manager Magazin, which first reported his death, Kühne is said to have returned from Mallorca to his Swiss home in Schindellegi ten days ago and to seek medical treatment.
Kühne and his wife Christine have no children. His fortune, which Bilanz estimated at between CHF21-22 billion in its annual list of the richest Swiss, is to pass to the Kühne Foundation following his death.

Syria sentences Assad-era mufti Hassoun to life imprisonment
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
09:41:40 UTC
18:41:40 KST

Breadcrumb
Syria sentences Assad-era mufti Ahmed Hassoun to life imprisonment
A Syrian court on Monday handed a life sentence to Ahmed Hassoun, the country's former grand mufti under ousted leader Bashar al-Assad, convicting him of crimes including inciting sectarian strife and exploiting his position.
Hassoun, the 10th Assad-era figure to be sentenced under the new authorities, was Syria's top Muslim cleric for 16 years.
He was known for his close ties to the former president and frequent appearances alongside him on religious occasions.
Judge Fakhr al-Din al-Aryan said Hassoun, 77, was guilty of a raft of charges including "inciting civil war and sectarian strife", for which he was jailed for life.
The cleric was also convicted of "incitement to intentional homicide", "principal complicity in intentional homicide", and "inciting sectarian and racial strife", for which he was handed additional terms ranging from three to 20 years.
The court also decided to confiscate Hassoun's assets and hand them to the public treasury.
His sentencing is the first against a religious figure since Syrian authorities began trying Assad-era officials in April.
On 11 August, Syria sentenced Bashar al-Assad, his brother Maher and five other security officials to death in absentia for atrocities committed during Syria's civil war, the first such ruling under the new authorities.
The former president fled Syria as his government fell in December 2024 and is believed to be in Russia.
Authorities have also handed death sentences to Atif Najib and Wassim al-Assad, cousins of the former ruler who were tried in person.
Hassoun, a native of Aleppo whose late father was also an important religious figure, was arrested at Damascus airport in March last year as he tried to flee the country.
Though he held the post of grand mufti for more than a decade, Hassoun lost the title in 2021 when Syria abolished the position.
The United Nations and human rights organisations have voiced opposition to the death sentences handed to Assad-era officials.
Human Rights Watch on Sunday said the sentences "raise important legal issues the government should urgently address".
"Advancing justice for the litany of serious crimes committed in Syria requires more than just convictions, but building a system that can deliver competent, impartial, and independent justice," said Balkees Jarrah, the group's Middle East and North Africa director.
Syria began legal proceedings in April against Bashar al-Assad and other officials accused of atrocities during the civil war, which erupted in 2011 with brutal repression of pro-democracy protesters.
More than half a million people were killed and millions displaced during the conflict, while tens of thousands disappeared.

The Israeli military carried out a new raid in the countryside of southern Syria's Daraa Monday, local media reported, a day after Damascus and Tel Aviv held a de-escalation meeting.
"Israeli occupation forces advanced with several military vehicles into the village of Maariya in the western Daraa countryside," Syrian Alikhbariah TV reported.
On Sunday, Israeli forces raided the town of al-Rafid in Quneitra province and arrested a shepherd, according to the channel.
Areas in southern Syria have witnessed near-daily Israeli incursions and attacks, particularly in Quneitra and Daraa provinces, including raids, searches, arrests and the establishment of military checkpoints.
The latest attacks come despite Syrian and Israeli officials met in Jordan for high-level U.S.-mediated talks in Jordan Sunday.
The meeting was aimed at easing tensions following recent Israeli strikes on Syrian territory, Syria's state news agency SANA reported, citing a diplomatic source at the Foreign Ministry.
The talks focused on practical mechanisms to halt Israeli strikes, arrests and targeted operations and on reviving negotiations toward a security agreement that could lay the groundwork for a broader future accord, SANA said.
"The meeting came as part of efforts aimed at reducing escalation following the latest Israeli shelling of Syrian territory and rising tensions in southern Syria," one diplomatic source said.
The two sides also discussed efforts to ease tensions between Israel and Türkiye.
Syria's Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani told Reuters Saturday that Damascus expected security negotiations with Israel to resume soon, although he added that there was a lack of trust between them.
Talks had been suspended since the start of the Iran war, while Syria cut off contact entirely after Israeli strikes on Syria’s Abu al-Duhur air base last week, according to al-Shaibani.
Washington has for more than a year sought to broker a security agreement between Israel and the government of Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.
Al-Shaibani said the two sides had agreed on paper to "almost everything” around the beginning of the year, including arrangements for security zones in southern Syria and a buffer zone where only United Nations forces would be present, but Damascus doubted Israel's willingness to implement the agreement.
The Israeli prime minister's office did not reply to a request for comment on al-Shaibani's remarks.
At Sunday’s meeting, SANA said, Syria indicated that its immediate priorities remained an Israeli withdrawal to positions held before Bashar Assad's overthrow on Dec. 8, 2024 and the full restoration of a 1974 disengagement agreement.
Damascus also told the Israeli delegation it would not accept arrangements restricting its right to rebuild and develop its armed forces or determine its alliances and partnerships, SANA said.
Syria reiterated that the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights were Syrian territory but said discussions over the region's final status were premature, according to the SANA report.
Israel has carried out repeated strikes on Syrian military sites since Assad's fall, claiming its actions were necessary to protect its security. Syria has denied posing a threat to Israel and has demanded an end to Israeli strikes and incursions.
Syria and Israel have technically been at war since 1948. Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the 1967 Six-Day War and later annexed it, a move recognized by the United States but not by most of the international community.

====================================================================================================

ann veronica janssens fills Hermès ginza with light, fog and shifting perception
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
09:35:32 UTC
18:35:32 KST

For her first solo exhibition in Japan, Ann Veronica Janssens is taking over Le Forum at Ginza Maison Hermès in Tokyo with things that are notoriously difficult to hang on a wall: light, air, time and perception itself. Titled 5 Chome 4-1 Ginza, Tokyo after the building’s own address, the exhibition opens on September 11, 2026, and brings together more than ten works conceived around the physical conditions of the space, alongside pieces from the artist’s ongoing practice since the 1990s.
Born in Folkestone in 1956 and based in Brussels, Janssens has spent decades testing how little an artwork might need in order to completely reorganize a room. After initially working with materials including plywood, glass and concrete, she increasingly turned toward light, sound and artificial fog around the beginning of the 1990s. Rather than filling architecture with objects, her installations tend to loosen its edges, using reflection, transparency and shifting atmospheric conditions to make space feel considerably less dependable than it did five minutes earlier.
Donut, 2003 | image: Florian Hölzherr, courtesy of CCA Wattis Institute for Contemporary Arts, San Francisco
LIGHT, GLITTER AND A SWING THAT REMEMBERS YOUR TOUCH
Among the works presented in Tokyo is Rose (2007), an installation in which seven spotlights cut through suspended particles, turning dispersed light into something that appears almost solid. Janssens repeatedly works in this uneasy zone between matter and immateriality, where a beam can behave like sculpture and an apparently empty room suddenly acquires thickness. In Untitled (blue glitter), open sculpture #1 (2015–2026), blue micro-glitter spreads across the floor, catching changing light and registering the fleeting effects of movement, viewpoint and time.
The body gets an even more direct role in Swings (2000–2023). Made from rope and wood, the suspended seats are covered with heat-sensitive film that changes through contact, allowing a visitor’s touch to briefly alter the work. Janssens has long resisted the idea of the viewer as a politely stationary observer: movement, interaction and the presence of other bodies become part of what is being exhibited. Here, looking is not quite enough — perception has to get up and move around.
Swings, 2002-2023 | image: Andrea Rossetti, courtesy of Pirelli Hangar Bicocca
AN INVISIBLE ARCHITECTURE TAKES OVER LE FORUM
Elsewhere, works including Donut extend the exhibition into projected light, duration and the less tangible materials that have defined Janssens’ practice. Taken together, the installations manipulate light, air and circulation to produce what the Fondation d’entreprise Hermès describes as a kind of invisible architecture: spaces generated not through walls and ceilings, but through changes in atmosphere and sensation. The title’s insistence on a precise street address makes that strategy particularly pointed, anchoring an exhibition dedicated to unstable perception to one very fixed point on the map.
Janssens’ experiments have often intersected with research into the relationship between space, time, the body and the brain, including through the Brain Space Laboratory, which she co-founded with Nathalie Ergino in 2009. At Ginza Maison Hermès, however, the experiment does not require much explanation. Glitter shifts, light gains volume, surfaces react and architecture becomes unexpectedly porous. 5 Chome 4-1 Ginza, Tokyo runs at Le Forum on the eighth and ninth floors of Ginza Maison Hermès through January 11, 2027, with free admission.

Russians have damaged 492 locomotives since start of full-scale war
Russian attacks have damaged 492 locomotives and 249 railway carriages since the start of the full-scale invasion. A government action programme envisages repairing 70% of the damaged locomotives.
Source: Rail.Insider
Details: Fifty-two employees of Ukrzaliznytsia (Ukrainian Railways) have been killed while carrying out their professional duties, and another 317 have been injured. Since the beginning of this year alone, Russia has attacked Ukraine's railway infrastructure 1,534 times, according to Mykola Kalashnyk, Ukraine's Minister for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport.
However, 70% of the damaged locomotives are to be repaired under the government's action programme.
The programme for 2026-2027 envisages reforming the railway transport system, expanding the European-gauge railway network, and introducing a new funding model for state-commissioned and socially important passenger services.
The programme also entails repairing 70% of damaged locomotives, renewing 10% of the railway's rolling stock and making 25 railway stations accessible.
Background:
- On 23 August, a Russian UAV struck a Lozova-Kharkiv electric train in Kharkiv Oblast, killing two people and injuring five others. The train had been evacuated, but some people were standing nearby at the time of the attack.
- Ukrzaliznytsia had previously said that the summer season would be more challenging than the previous one, as demand was rising while the number of passenger carriages had fallen: Russian forces had destroyed 46 carriages and damaged another 200 since the start of the full-scale invasion.
- In 2025, Ukraine's railways transported 161.3 million tonnes of freight – 13.6 million tonnes, or 7.8%, less than in 2024.
- Ukrzaliznytsia has signed a contract with the Kriukiv Railway Car Building Works for the supply of another 92 new passenger carriages.
- French manufacturer Alstom and Ukrzaliznytsia have agreed on the supply of 55 modern freight locomotives worth €475 million to Ukraine.

They Dedicated Their Lives to Teaching. Then the Deepfakes Started
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
09:30:00 UTC
18:30:00 KST

For Luis DeSantiago, a substitute teacher in Los Banos, California, it started with a few text messages. On March 12, as he was working his other part-time job at a coffee shop, his phone lit up. A fellow barista said there was an AI photo circulating on social media. Her cousin wanted to know if it was DeSantiago.
At first, DeSantiago wasn’t worried—he figured that inappropriate photos violated TikTok’s community guidelines and were usually quickly removed.
“When I finally saw the image, that’s when it felt like a punch to the gut,” DeSantiago tells WIRED. Parts of it resembled a mirror selfie that he remembered taking at a job in college. But instead of his work uniform, he was wearing lingerie. And instead of standing normally, as he had been in the original photo, he was posing suggestively.
The texts kicked off a monthslong saga that crossed two schools and involved students and administrators. And DeSantiago is far from the only educator who’s been victimized this way.
WIRED spoke with three other teachers who allege that their students made sexualized photos and videos of them, likely using AI. They say the incidents have been profoundly distressing and disappointing—and in some cases, it’s led them to reassess how they view their work and their relationships with their students.
“This Could Include Other Students”
After he received the texts, DeSantiago began to piece together who might have been behind the image. One account that shared it used their real name in their TikTok profile—it was a student DeSantiago knew from the local middle school, where he regularly filled in. DeSantiago suspected the involvement of two other students based on people who followed and interacted with that account, and his knowledge of student friend groups. He was scheduled to work at that very middle school the next day.
DeSantiago reported the incident to the assistant principal, who assured him that the school would "take care of it.” Later that evening, he decided to look for the image by searching his name on TikTok. He discovered that a different student had created an account impersonating him—it used his name, slightly mispelled, and had the same photo as their profile picture.
Over the next few weeks, DeSantiago says, he went back and forth with school administrators, the parents of the students, and even the police.
“If these students aren't afraid of generating and posting these images of me, I am concerned of what they may be circulating privately through text messages and group chats,” DeSantiago wrote to the principal. “Keep in mind this could include other students as well.”
One student, who admitted to creating the image, was disciplined with in-school suspension. DeSantiago was later told that the image was also shared on Snapchat. But DeSantiago says the image continued to proliferate, and other students began posting it. He says he also received several crude, sexual comments on his TikTok account.
DeSantiago told administrators he didn’t want to take assignments at the middle school “until this matter is fully addressed.” The district did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment.
He took a substitute assignment at the local high school, but the problems followed him. During one class, he received an AirDropped photo of the same AI-generated image before it was quickly revoked. He could tell it was circulating among the class.
The principal told him the school was launching an “immediate investigation” and offered to meet with DeSantiago or make the school counselor available, but DeSantiago says he probably won’t return to the district this year.
He tells WIRED that, at least right now, he doesn’t feel safe doing so.
“It Makes You Question Everything”
When fake nude images of nonconsenting adults are disseminated, it could constitute cyberstalking and violate the federal Take It Down Act, which makes it a crime to publish nonconsensual “intimate visual depictions of individuals, both authentic and computer-generated,” on the internet.
In most of the accounts shared with WIRED, the teachers didn't directly report the content to the platforms on which it appeared. Snap spokesperson Monique Bellamy shared the company's policies on harassment and sexual content, which prohibit sharing AI-generated or manipulated content to humiliate or sexually harass others. She told WIRED that the company has "established processes" for reporting such content, and that it continues to "develop features and tools designed to support the safety, privacy, and well-being of our community." TikTok did not provide comment before publication.
Donna Ballman, a retired employment advocacy lawyer, tells WIRED that if a student creates and shares sexual images of a teacher, it constitutes a “clear case” of sexual harassment in the workplace.
Ballman says that under federal antidiscrimination laws, employers have an obligation to create a workplace free of sexual harassment. In a school, this could mean disciplining the student or moving them to a different classroom. She adds, however, that there's “no blueprint” for how schools need to respond to these incidents. Administrators don’t even have to tell a victimized teacher how a student may have been disciplined.
“They just have to make [and] create a safe environment for the victim,” Ballman says.
One middle school teacher in her mid-twenties tells WIRED that she’s seen so much AI-generated content used to harass teachers that she’s bracing for the next wave. (She requested anonymity because she did not have permission from her school district to speak about her experience.)
Last year, she says, students found public photos of a teacher in her sixties, manipulated them to make it appear that she was committing sex acts, and shared them with each other in a Snapchat group chat.
A few months ago, the teacher says, she learned from a student about a TikTok account impersonating her. It looked AI-generated—her face had the characteristic smoothness of AI-generated content, her mouth was moving unnaturally while speaking, and the sound of her voice didn’t match her own. Some of the videos showed her doing things like skydiving or backflips. But others depicted her talking about sexual acts she performed and enjoyed.
She says she told her principal about the account and that they assured her that they would “see what we can do.” Throughout the day, students continued to warn her about the account. She says that some told her that they knew who made the account—one of their classmates. She says the student was known to have behavioral problems.
“I know a lot of the kids that reported it to me genuinely believed that was my account, and that I was saying those things,” she tells WIRED. “I was like, ‘Oh my god, you guys—that is not me.’” She asked them to report it to TikTok, and she says the account was quickly taken down.
Still unnerved by the incident, she mentioned the TikTok account during the next monthly teacher meeting. A colleague said he had seen a seemingly AI-generated fake video of himself getting arrested, which he believed was generated by the same student.
As days and weeks passed, she says, she became the target of escalating, in-person harassment from this same student, who began “cursing me out, calling me names, telling me to fuck off, calling me a bitch.” She raised it at the next faculty meeting, and the assistant principal said that the same student was calling and texting them in the middle of the night and posting apparent AI-generated photos of them to TikTok.
She says the principal removed the student from her class and tried to limit his access to her. But she says that the harassment continued until the student ultimately left the district, and TikTok removed the account.
She says that these behavioral issues aren’t exclusive to this particular student. “It's kind of unsurprising that we are dealing with that, because these kids just have a hard time,” she says. "I'm just worried about this happening again.”
Other teachers say their experiences have fundamentally changed the way they relate to students.
Alice, who asked to be identified by her first name, works for a UK college that trains students aged 16 to 19 in trades like construction. Her job combines administrative responsibilities, like taking attendance, with the role of a college counselor. She says she individually meets with about 150 students throughout the year and takes pride in being able to be a sounding board, give them advice, and serve as a mentor.
This winter, she says, school administrators told her that a student filed a report claiming two videos were circulating among his classmates. One appeared to be real, and it showed her having a conversation with a student. The other one, they said, appeared to be a manipulated version of the first. But instead of talking to the student, it showed her taking her clothes off and dancing around in what was either underwear or a bikini.
Alice tells WIRED that as a qualified youth worker, part of her job often involves talking about things that students may feel “too embarrassed to tell their parents about,” like drugs, parties, or having safe sex. She says she had several of those conversations with the student she suspected had created the video. The student denied it when questioned by administrators and soon dropped out of the school. (The college did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment.)
“It makes me reflect as well on those conversations, thinking, did he think that he could overstep a line because we were having these discussions?” she says. “It makes you question everything,” she says.
Afterward, the college gave her permission to step away from the class for a few weeks and took steps to educate students about the danger of creating or distributing deepfakes. But when she returned, she says, the atmosphere had chilled.
“I did have a really good rapport with my students—I do have a good rapport with my students,” she says. And she still loves her work. “But it's definitely made me a bit more cautious, a bit more vigilant when it comes to folks.”
“It Crosses the Line”
Like DeSantiago, Arizona-based sixth-grade teacher Luke Red says his students circulated an AI-generated photo of him in the comments of his public TikTok account. The image depicted him and another male teacher kissing each other.
Red says he reported the accounts to TikTok—not for content violations but for being under the minimum age of 13—but says TikTok didn’t remove the accounts. He says that the school immediately launched an investigation and quickly identified the student, who admitted to creating and sharing the image. The student received a three-day suspension—the most severe punishment kids their age can receive for a first-time sexual harassment offense, according to the school district handbook. The district did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment.
Red tells WIRED that reflecting on the experience “has kind of sent me into a spiral.” His concerns, he says, are not necessarily about what happened to him. They’re more focused on the enthusiastic, permissive culture surrounding AI use among his students.
“It just got to the point where students felt comfortable enough creating inappropriate images,” Red says. “Obviously when you're making your teachers do sexual things with these images, that's where it crosses the line.”
Ultimately, he feels more sorry for the students than for himself.
“It's just clear [that] so many kids nowadays just don't understand not only how what they're doing can affect others, but just what happens on the internet and how dangerous it can be,” Red says.

The UK will stand with you in the darkness and in the light. The UK Prime Minister column
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
12:29:00 EEST
18:29:00 KST

The UK will stand with you in the darkness and in the light. The UK Prime Minister column
The blue and yellow flag will today fly defiantly across Ukraine, yet its people were never meant to commemorate this moment again. For 1,643 days of full-scale invasion, Putin has tried to erase this anniversary from your calendar. And for 1,643 days, Ukrainians have made it impossible for him to succeed.
I know that has not come without cost.
Today, Ukrainian children will study underground, and their parents will put them to bed fearful for what horror the night might bring.
Ukrainian servicemen and women will risk everything to defend the line between reason and violence.
And countless Ukrainians will find the courage to carry on in the names of those lost to this senseless war.
On the 35th anniversary of the restoration of your independence, the British people stand in solidarity with the free people of Ukraine.
We pay tribute to every Ukrainian fighting to maintain your right to live in a country of your own making. And we honour those who have given their lives so that others will know that future.
On a personal note, I would like to assure the people of Ukraine that while there has been a change of leadership in Britain, there will be no change in our support for Ukraine. President Zelenskyy was the first world leader I hosted as Prime Minister.
Today, Ukraine becomes the first country I visit as Prime Minister.
I want this to serve as a statement that Britain remains your most committed, most reliable friend.
We all know true friends offer more than words. The UK will provide Ukraine with €3.5 billion a year of military support for as long as it takes. At the Ankara Summit, together with NATO Allies, we pledged €70 billion in military assistance, equipment and training for Ukraine this year – and the same again next year.
Make no mistake, Putin sees these numbers as a signal that Ukraine’s friends are sticking around.
I am acutely aware this is no moment for self-congratulation. Night after night, Russia continues its brutal pounding of your homeland with drones and missiles. Last winter was punishing. Russian attacks plunged towns and cities into darkness and cold.
Preparations for the next have already begun and Ukraine desperately needs its partners to dig deep – into their stockpiles and their pockets – to provide the air defence systems and energy support needed to protect lives, homes and infrastructure. The UK will be at the forefront of that effort.
We will stand with Ukraine every day your fight lasts. We will be with you long after it concludes. For more than a year, the Coalition of the Willing has convened dozens of countries to form a plan for how a Ukraine-led peace deal will be sustained. And today, I am proud to take up co-leadership of the Coalition alongside President Macron and Chancellor Merz.
Britain will never mistake who is bearing the burden of this terrible war and the support we provide will always be unconditional. The people of Ukraine do not owe Europe anything, it is Europe who owes the people of Ukraine everything – you are not only defending your own freedom, you are defending ours as well.
This war was never only about the fate of one nation. If one authoritarian can violate international law, abuse every standard of human decency and redraw a border by force, then others will be tempted to do the same. What happens in Ukraine matters to the whole of Europe, it matters to the rest of the world.
It has been said that 24 February 2022 was the date of the second referendum on Ukrainian independence. The world saw how the people of Ukraine answered and it inspires us to this day still. It is a cruel irony that you are forced to mark your independence under the pain of conflict once again. This is a war you did not choose but from which you refuse to back down.
For our part, Britain will not forget about Ukraine.
Our hundred-year partnership is a commitment to the long term. We will not tire. We will not turn away.
The time will come when Ukrainians gather to celebrate independence free to live in peace and prosperity. And when that moment arrives, Britain will be there: proud to have stood with you in the darkness, ready to build a future with you in the light.
From our nation to yours, Happy Independence Day – and Glory to Ukraine.
Andy Burnham,
The UK Prime Minister

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taiwan Deputy Representative to the Philippines Lee Ting-sheng (李廷盛) said Taiwan wants stronger regional cooperation on climate change and disaster response, CNA reported Monday.
Speaking at the conference “Towards a Peaceful and Sustainable Future: Addressing Climate and Conflict in ASEAN,” hosted by the Stratbase Institute and the German Embassy in the Philippines, Lee said extreme weather had become an urgent regional threat.
Lee said the Philippines, Taiwan, and Japan are on the front line of climate change. He called for closer cooperation to improve disaster preparedness and emergency response.
He said cooperation could focus on three areas: sharing weather warnings in real time, exchanging smart-governance technology, and strengthening regional resilience. He said these measures could help governments respond more quickly to extreme weather.
Lee also proposed a cross-border humanitarian assistance system involving Taiwan, the Philippines, Japan, and other partners along the first island chain. He said such a system could reduce disaster damage and strengthen security and prosperity in the western Pacific.
Taiwan and the Philippines have cooperated on weather monitoring and disaster prevention since the 2000s. Taiwan has helped the Philippines establish an upper-air observation station, more than 10 automated weather stations, and an information display center to improve typhoon tracking and forecasting.
The two sides also launched the VOTE research program in 2016. The program focuses on volcanoes, oceans, typhoons, and earthquakes.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Kaohsiung City Government’s Water Resources Bureau defended its progress on flood mitigation after the National Audit Office criticized the city for slowly implementing measures proposed following Typhoon Gaemi.
The National Audit Office said the city had completed fewer than 20% of the 59 flood mitigation measures proposed after the typhoon, per UDN. It reported that the city government had failed to purchase mobile water pumps on schedule and that maintenance records for existing equipment contained errors.
The office also noted that 19 of the 59 measures still lacked funding as of the end of 2025. It highlighted several flood mitigation facilities that had remained in disrepair for years.
The Water Resources Bureau said emergency repairs and other measures implemented after Gaemi had helped reduce the impact of recent heavy rainfall, per Newtalk. It explained that flood mitigation projects are designed to provide medium- to long-term improvements and therefore require more time to complete.
Regarding funding shortages, damaged facilities, and the delayed purchase of mobile water pumps, the bureau said its budget was limited but that it would continue monitoring the situation and making improvements.
The bureau also faced criticism from opposition politicians. Kaohsiung City Councilor Chen Mei-ya (陳美雅) urged the city government to determine why flooding remained a problem despite roughly NT$580 million (US$18.21 million) having been invested in flood-mitigation projects, per UDN.
KMT Legislator Ko Chih-en (柯志恩) visited Dianbao Village in Kaohsiung’s Ziguan District and called on the government to reassess flood mitigation measures in the area, per Liberty Times. She urged a comprehensive review of the village’s infrastructure, saying it had experienced repeated flooding.
In response to Chen’s criticism, the bureau said mitigation measures had reduced the areas affected by flooding but warned that engineering solutions have limitations when faced with extreme rainfall.
In a related development, department stores across Kaohsiung remained open despite the city’s suspension of work and classes, drawing criticism from workers, per CNA. Employees said that even E-DA Theme Park, located in a mountainous area of Kaohsiung, did not allow workers to take the day off.
The theme park said employees could request breaks if flooding or other safety concerns prevented them from working. Two minor landslides occurred Sunday on a road leading to the theme park, per SETN.

The estimated annual growth rate of 46% is higher than the roughly 30% expected for AI high-performance computing chips, per CTEE.

Other recently popular sectors, including printed circuit boards, shipping, passive components, and optical communications, also saw profit-taking. Among PCB stocks, APCB hit its daily limit down, while Glotech Industrial fell nearly 9%. In optical communications, LandMark Optoelectronics, Visual Photonics Epitaxy, and LuxNet all declined more than 5%.
Analyst Yang Huei-yu (楊惠宇) said the market had recently been weighed down by profit-taking and selling by investors seeking to cut losses on shares purchased at higher prices. With trading volume falling, the TAIEX is likely to remain in consolidation as investors assess their next moves.
She said the recent consolidation could help clear out weaker positions and lay the groundwork for a recovery. Yang expects individual stocks to remain the focus until the broader market shows clearer signs of recovery and trading activity picks up, per CTEE.
